item.title: Day Around the Bay: The Castro Theatre’s Long-Awaited New Organ Has Arrived
item.description: Super Bowl tickets are hitting the event’s second-highest price ever; a Waymo hit an elementary school student in SoCal; and the Castro Theatre's much-anticipated new digital organ has arrived and will soon make its debut.

item.title: Friday Morning Constitutional: Super Bowl to Bring Street Closures Galore
item.description: Today is another nationwide day of protest against ICE; former CNN anchor Don Lemon was arrested by federal agents over a protest; and various events will be causing street closures around SF for the Super Bowl next week.

item.title: Biennial Homeless Census Shifts to Morning Count In Hopes of Better Accuracy
item.description: Outreach workers and volunteers fanned out across San Francisco Thursday morning conducting this year's biennial point-in-time count of the homeless.

item.title: Man Charged With Attempted Murder Over Bizarre Car Chase That Almost Killed SFPD Officer in Oakland
item.description: An SFPD officer assigned to Oakland was nearly killed on the job Tuesday, in an eventful car chase that featured a murder attempt, a wrong-way chase on I-580, and Oakland Police opening fire for reasons even they can’t explain.

item.title: Anthropic Signs Lease For Entire 27-Story Downtown Tower
item.description: Anthropic, the growing AI concern founded by two siblings and former OpenAI execs, had inked a deal for an entire office building at Howard and Fremont streets, marking one of the largest office deals in the city since 2019.

item.title: Super Bowl Drone Ban Declared at Several SF Locations, in Addition to Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara
item.description: It’s no surprise that drones are banned from the Super Bowl at Levi’s Stadium, but that ban has also been curiously extended to SF venues like the Ferry Building, the Moscone Center, and even Grace Cathedral.

item.title: Update: West Oakland BART Station Reopens After Train Collided With Person
item.description: A major medical emergency stemming from a person possibly being struck by a BART train shut down West Oakland Station Friday afternoon, and service was being impacted throughout the system.

item.title: Gavin Newsom Goes on Attack Against Dr. Oz Over Inflammatory Video Accusing LA Armenians of Mafia Fraud
item.description: Dr Oz’s latest conspiracy theory says that the “Russian Armenia mafia” is running fake hospice centers in LA, and Gavin Newsom is taking legal action, as many of the businesses Oz highlights aren’t even hospice care.

item.title: Salinas Man Throws Doberman Puppy at Cops to Evade Arrest, Still Gets Arrested Anyway
item.description: A poor little stolen Doberman puppy was not only dognapped by a man allegedly carrying 68 grams of meth, the puppy was then used as a weapon and thrown at Monterey County Sheriff’s deputies when they tried to arrest the man.

item.title: Day Around the Bay: SF’s Archbishop Riordan High School Goes Online Amid Tuberculosis Cases
item.description: Students and workers across the Bay Area took part in a nationwide walkout Friday; Yosemite eliminated the reservation system for Firefall and will instead be limiting car and foot traffic; and classes will be held remotely at SF’s Archbishop Riordan High School to cut the spread of TB.
